verdicts.detail: All stated details match. (1) Web Worker: blast-worker.js is instantiated as a Worker at script.js:20712, and its header (line 4) says it runs as a Web Worker. (2) Downloads and caches in IndexedDB: ensureDb() fetches the FASTA on first use (line 772 fetch(dbUrl), with the 'downloading (first time only)' progress message) and stores it in IndexedDB via idbPut (lines 777-778); subsequent lookups read from the IDB cache ('loading from cache' line 765, 'loading cached index' line 751). (3) First query slower than subsequent ones: first query downloads+indexes; later queries hit the cache (DB_SEQS short-circuits at line 724, cached text/index reuse). (4) Smith-Waterman local alignment: scoring uses smithWatermanAffine()/smithWatermanAffineBanded() (lines 170, 309), actually invoked in the search path (lines 611, 629); the DP is local — M[rowBase]=0 reset (line 214) and 'best=0, dir=0' local restart (line 230) with the comment 'restart (local alignment)' (line 227). The Gotoh affine-gap refinement is a standard Smith-Waterman variant, consistent with the manual's general 'Smith-Waterman local alignment' wording.

note: Claim 15 verified as MATCH: blast-worker.js runs as a Web Worker (script.js:20712), downloads FASTA on first use and caches it (plus the built index) in IndexedDB (IDB_NAME='blast-db-cache-v1'; fetch at line 772, idbPut at 777-778; cache reads at 765/751), making the first query slower than subsequent cached ones, and scoring uses smithWatermanAffine/smithWatermanAffineBanded which implement local alignment via the M[rowBase]=0 reset and best=0/dir=0 local restart (lines 214, 227, 230).
